basis: Original Godot material remains visible under 13 high-contrast debug-color overlays; each species is shown from front, three-quarter and side views.
metric_note: Precision/recall/F1 are strict visual estimates for boundary triage, not pixel-ground-truth measurements. Precision asks whether colored pixels belong to the defined target; recall asks whether the visible target is covered; F1 is the harmonic mean.

palette_change.purpose: Separate diagnostic readability from geometry accuracy.
palette_change.result: Successful: all 13 regions are distinguishable in the three-view plates. This changes no region boundary and earns no geometry score by itself.

regions.reason: The cyan cap is visible, but the front view is wider than the single central upward tuft and the side view loses a clean tuft boundary.
regions.next_action: Narrow x and y to the protruding tuft silhouette; exclude the crown instead of relying on a broad height band.

regions.reason: The orange rectangle crosses both brows and the upper eye area, violating the definition that the zone is only between the brows and above the eyes.
regions.next_action: Shrink the x radius and tighten the y/depth window; use the brow gap as the center, not a full forehead strip.

regions.reason: The yellow dog ear flap is mostly the intended outer ear body, but it reaches the lower/outer edge and overlaps the tip candidate.
regions.next_action: Keep the main flap, subtract the tip band, and trim the lower cheek-facing edge.

regions.reason: The lime color reads as a long outer-ear rim rather than only the uppermost/outermost tip.
regions.next_action: Reduce the vertical span and make the tip threshold species/ear-shape aware.

regions.reason: The green blocks reach around the eyes and down toward the mouth corners; the defined cheek fluff is the side muzzle fur below the eyes and beside the nose, excluding those identity features.
regions.next_action: Use a narrower side contour and subtract eye, nose and mouth protection zones.

regions.reason: The magenta region is a large neck bib: it covers the neck, shoulders and much more than the user-circled upper heart-shaped tuft. A 70 score is not defensible.
regions.next_action: Remove the broad lower band; keep only the upper heart lobes and short center point inside the circled tuft.

regions.reason: The blue area is a rectangular full belly/hip block and reaches the leg-root area, while the definition excludes chest, leg roots and tail.
regions.next_action: Replace the rectangle with a tapered central belly contour and stop above the leg split.

regions.reason: The violet area sits mainly on the upper arm/shoulder; it does not represent the full forearm and paw, and it conflicts with the elbow band.
regions.next_action: Anchor the region between the elbow and paw, then subtract the elbow cuff rather than using one broad y band.

regions.reason: The red stripe is readable but looks like an artificial horizontal stripe and is not consistently centered on the anatomical elbow in all views.
regions.next_action: Move the band to the actual elbow bend and reduce its height/side spill.

regions.reason: The pink lower-leg area is broadly in the right place, but it stops/bleeds inconsistently around the foot and knee transition.
regions.next_action: Separate the foot silhouette from the knee cuff and follow the lower-leg/foot surface rather than a rectangular height band.

regions.reason: The cyan knee ring is not visually localized as a knee ring in the front or side plate; it is mostly hidden by other broad regions.
regions.next_action: Temporarily disable this candidate until a joint-centered mask is defined from the leg bend, then render it alone for approval.

regions.reason: The dog side view has no readable lime tail-tip region; the current threshold misses the visible dog tail end.
regions.next_action: Use a dog-specific tail axis/endpoint mask; do not reuse the fox tail depth thresholds.

regions.reason: The slate area becomes a distal tail block/tip instead of the lower-side surface and is not separated cleanly from the tail end.
regions.next_action: Define the underside relative to the dog tail's local vertical direction and exclude the endpoint.

regions.reason: The cyan head-tuft region is not readable in any of the three fox views; the current dog-derived threshold does not isolate the fox's tiny central tuft.
regions.next_action: Create a fox-specific tuft locator and use a contrasting diagnostic color; do not infer correctness from the absence of color.

regions.reason: The orange band is too wide and reaches the brow/eye neighborhood instead of staying in the central forehead gap.
regions.next_action: Narrow the center and tighten the depth/height window above the eyes.

regions.reason: The yellow overlay mostly follows the fox outer/back ear and the inner white fur remains protected, which matches the definition; the lower/outer edge still overlaps the tip candidate.
regions.next_action: Keep the source-texture white-ear guard and subtract a smaller, explicit tip region.

regions.reason: The lime overlay is visible at the ear ends but extends down the outer rim instead of remaining only at the top/outermost tip.
regions.next_action: Shorten the tip band along the ear axis and exclude the main outer-ear body.

regions.reason: The green region covers a broad mask beside and partly around the eyes, not only the cheek/muzzle fluff; it also cuts into the white transition.
regions.next_action: Follow the cheek silhouette below the eye and subtract eye, nose, mouth and white-muzzle protection areas.

regions.reason: The magenta region is a neck-to-chest bib and includes the neck/shoulder transition, far beyond the circled upper heart-shaped chest tuft.
regions.next_action: Remove the long lower component and keep only the small upper heart tuft.

regions.reason: The blue region is a broad rectangular belly panel extending toward the hips/leg roots, not a central belly surface bounded below the chest.
regions.next_action: Use a tapered belly contour and stop before the leg split and tail junction.

regions.reason: The violet region captures the upper arm more than the forearm/paw and overlaps the elbow transition.
regions.next_action: Anchor it to the lower arm/paw surface and subtract the elbow cuff.

regions.reason: The red bands are visible, but they read as arbitrary stripes rather than a joint-centered transition ring in every view.
regions.next_action: Use the elbow bend and local limb axis; reduce the band width.

regions.reason: The pink lower-leg candidate is broadly located, but the foot boundary and knee transition are not clean.
regions.next_action: Separate foot/lower-leg coverage from the knee cuff and follow the actual limb silhouette.

regions.reason: The cyan knee region is not a clear knee ring in the three views and is largely swallowed by the broad leg/belly candidates.
regions.next_action: Redefine from the joint bend and validate as a single-region render before restoring it to the plate.

regions.reason: The lime fox tail tip is clearly visible in the three-quarter and side views and stays at the actual endpoint; it is the strongest current local-region candidate.
regions.next_action: Keep as a candidate, then inspect the soft edge and ensure the tip does not include the upper tail plane.

regions.reason: The slate overlay forms a block on the distal tail rather than a coherent lower-side strip and is too close to the tip.
regions.next_action: Define the underside in the fox tail's local frame and subtract the tip before judging it again.

round_findings: High-contrast colors make all 13 candidates readable; this is a diagnostic success only, not a boundary success.
The previous chest_tuft scores were invalid because visibility/recall was mistaken for precision. Both species must reject the current chest mask.
The next geometry patch must prioritize chest_tuft, forehead_mark_zone, cheek_fluff and belly_center; only after those are narrowed should arm/leg joint bands be revisited.
Fox ear_pair and fox tail_tip are the only current local candidates close to approval; fox head_tuft is not validated because it is not visible.
Dog tail regions require species-specific coordinates; reusing fox-like depth thresholds is not acceptable.
